title: Separable-closure Cech coordinates for continuous coefficient modules
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $k^s/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. Put $G_k=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. The morphism $v:\operatorname{Spec}k^s\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a covering in the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Its $(q+1)$-fold fibre product, for every integer $q\geq0$, identifies over $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\times G_k^q$, where the latter means the inverse limit of the finite disjoint unions indexed by finite quotients of $G_k^q$. The face maps are those of the usual group Cech nerve, with the convention that the descent cocycle equation is $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$.

Let $A$ be any nonarchimedean normed field, with its metric topology, and put $R_{A,T}=p_T^*\underline A$, $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Then
$$\Gamma((\operatorname{Spec}k^s)^{q+1}_{/k},R_A)=C(G_k^q,A)$$
canonically, compatibly with face maps and continuous field homomorphisms. On $(\operatorname{Spec}k^s)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ every lisse $R_A$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module, sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is isomorphic to $R_A^{\oplus n}$ for some finite $n\geq0$. Moreover
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R_A}(R_A^{\oplus n},R_A^{\oplus m})=M_{m\times n}(A)$$
by constant matrices, including $m=0$ or $n=0$. For a continuous field map $A\to B$, scalar extension on these free modules and on the displayed Cech rings is entrywise postcomposition, using ordinary internal module scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Neither completeness nor algebraic closedness of the coefficient field $A$ is required.

source.place: Section 4.2, Lemma 4.2.12 (continuous-function sheaves), Section 7.3, Lemma 7.3.9 over a field, and the generic-field observation in Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71; agent expansion of the separable-closure Cech calculation. Also Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach, Example 3.1, p. 6.

proof.text: Put $\Omega=k^s$. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-cover-finite-coordinates] to obtain the singleton pro-etale cover, the directed finite Galois stages and their compatible incremental tensor isomorphisms $\theta_{E,q}$. This includes degree zero and supplies exactly the hypotheses of the next step.

source.place: Agent expansion of Bhatt–Scholze Example 4.1.4 and Definition 4.1.1; Stacks fields.tex Tag 0BU2 (lemma-infinite-galois-limit), pione.tex Tag 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois); finite-stage incremental tensor formula. Returned item proof steps 1–2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-galois-limit-nerve-faces] to those $\theta_{E,q}$. It gives $W_q\cong\Omega[G_k^q]$ over the first vertex, with all face and degeneracy formulas. In particular deleting the interior vertex of a triple multiplies successive increments as $gh$, so the descent equation is $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$.

source.place: Agent expansion of Stacks fields.tex Tag 0BU2 (lemma-infinite-galois-limit), algebra.tex Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits), limits.tex Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit); explicit cumulative-vertex substitution. Returned item proof steps 3–4.

proof.text: With these coordinates apply [lem-sfb-galois-continuous-section-naturality] for $A$, and for $B$ when a continuous field map $\varphi:A\to B$ is given. This gives both displayed section-ring coordinates, their face compatibility, and postcomposition by $\varphi$; at the point the section ring and coefficient map are $A$ and $\varphi$. It also identifies $v^*R_{A,k}$ with $R_{A,\Omega}$.

source.place: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1, p. 6; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 4.2.12; agent expansion of adjoint-normalized coefficient naturality and geometric-point evaluation. Returned item proof steps 5 and 9.

proof.text: The field $\Omega$ is separably closed. Apply [lem-sfb-separably-closed-lisse-split-trivialization] with $\Lambda=\underline A$ to any lisse trivializing cover. Its splitting section pulls the given slice trivialization back to $L\cong R_{A,\Omega}^{\oplus n}$ on the entire site, allowing $n=0$.

source.place: Bhatt–Scholze Section 2.4 (Lemma 2.4.8) and Example 7.3.5; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 0982 (lemma-w-local-strictly-henselian-extremally-disconnected); agent restriction of a slice trivialization along a splitting section. Returned item proof steps 6–7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-free-matrix-scalar-extension] on $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to $R=R_{A,\Omega}$, $S=R_{B,\Omega}$ and the coefficient morphism. Its hypotheses hold: $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is the final object of its own small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], whose size and sheafification conventions are those under which the internal/sectionwise module equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies; $R_{A,\Omega}$, $R_{B,\Omega}$ are commutative ring objects and $p_\Omega^*\varphi_*$ is a ring-object morphism. Step 3 identifies their global section rings with $A,B$ and their induced map with $\varphi$. Thus its matrices are exactly the constant $A$-matrices, and ordinary internal scalar extension gives the entrywise $\varphi$-matrix. Zero ranks are included. All inputs allowed arbitrary nonarchimedean normed fields, so no completeness or coefficient algebraic closedness was used.

source.place: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1, p. 6; elementary global-basis calculation and explicit balanced-map calculation for ordinary internal coequalizer scalar extension. Returned item proof steps 8 and 10, stated for a general ringed site.
